subject: AP Statistics
stem: A company claims that 40% of its customers renew their subscription. A random sample of 150 customers, a small fraction of all customers, shows that 33% renewed. A manager tests H0: p = 0.40 versus Ha: p < 0.40 at the 5% significance level. Which choice gives the correct test statistic, p-value and conclusion?

choices.t: z ≈ −1.75 and p ≈ 0.08, so there is not convincing evidence that fewer than 40% of customers renew.
z ≈ −1.75 and p ≈ 0.04, so there is convincing evidence that fewer than 40% of customers renew.
z ≈ −1.75 and p ≈ 0.04, so there is a 4% probability that the company's claim is true.
z ≈ −1.75 and p ≈ 0.96, so there is not convincing evidence that fewer than 40% of customers renew.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: A supplier claims that 30% of its parts are defective. A random sample of 250 parts, a small fraction of the shipment, has 35% defective. An inspector tests H0: p = 0.30 versus Ha: p ≠ 0.30 at the 5% significance level. Which choice gives the correct test statistic, p-value and conclusion?

choices.t: z ≈ 1.72 and p ≈ 0.042, so there is convincing evidence that the proportion differs from 0.30.
z ≈ 1.72 and p ≈ 0.085, so the data prove that the proportion is 0.30.
z ≈ 1.66 and p ≈ 0.098, so there is not convincing evidence that the proportion differs from 0.30.
z ≈ 1.72 and p ≈ 0.085, so there is not convincing evidence that the proportion differs from 0.30.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: A town claims that 50% of voters support a measure. A random sample of 400 voters, a small fraction of all voters, has 54.5% in support. A researcher tests H0: p = 0.50 versus Ha: p > 0.50 at the 1% significance level. Which choice gives the correct test statistic, p-value and conclusion?

choices.t: z ≈ 1.80 and p ≈ 0.036, so there is not convincing evidence that more than 50% support the measure.
z ≈ 1.80 and p ≈ 0.036, so there is convincing evidence that more than 50% support the measure.
z ≈ 1.80 and p ≈ 0.072, so there is not convincing evidence that more than 50% support the measure.
z ≈ 0.09 and p ≈ 0.46, so there is not convincing evidence that more than 50% support the measure.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: A phone maker claims that 25% of its phones need a repair within a year. In a random sample of 120 phones, a small fraction of all phones, 18% needed a repair. For H0: p = 0.25 versus Ha: p < 0.25, the p-value is about 0.038. Which statement correctly interprets this p-value?

choices.t: There is a 3.8% probability that the true proportion is 0.25.
The probability that exactly 18% of a sample of 120 phones need a repair is 3.8%.
If the true proportion were 0.25, about 3.8% of samples of 120 phones would have a proportion of 0.18 or lower.
There is a 3.8% probability that the true proportion is less than 0.25.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: Two independent random samples, each a small fraction of its population, are used to test H0: p1 − p2 = 0. Sample 1 has 6 successes out of 40 and sample 2 has 9 successes out of 50. Which statement about the large counts condition for the two-proportion z-test is correct?

choices.t: The condition is met, because each sample has at least 5 successes.
The condition is not met, because with the pooled proportion 15/90 ≈ 0.167, the expected successes are 40(0.167) ≈ 6.7 and 50(0.167) ≈ 8.3, both less than 10.
The condition is met, because both sample sizes are at least 30.
The condition is not met, because the sample proportions 0.15 and 0.18 are not equal.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: An analyst takes an independent random sample of 40 workers from a plant of 300 workers and a sample of 50 workers from a plant of 600 workers, and plans a two-proportion z-test of H0: p1 − p2 = 0. In sample 1, 18 workers are satisfied; in sample 2, 25 are satisfied. Which condition is NOT met?

choices.t: The independence (10%) condition for sample 1, because 40 is more than 10% of 300.
The large counts condition, because 18 is less than 25.
The random condition, because the plants have different sizes.
All conditions are met, because both samples are random.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: A statistician carries out a two-proportion z-test of H0: p1 − p2 = 0 and uses the pooled proportion in the standard error. Which statement best explains why the pooled proportion is used for the test?

choices.t: The pooled proportion is always closer to the true value than either sample proportion, even when H0 is false.
If H0 is true, both samples come from populations with the same proportion, so the combined sample gives the best single estimate of that proportion.
Pooling always makes the standard error larger, which guarantees that the test is conservative.
The pooled proportion is also used for confidence intervals, so the test and the interval must agree.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: Volunteers are randomly assigned to two treatments: 30 of 60 improve with treatment 1 and 28 of 70 improve with treatment 2. A student plans a two-proportion z-test of H0: p1 − p2 = 0. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: The conditions are met: the treatments were randomly assigned and, with the pooled proportion 58/130 ≈ 0.446, all expected counts are at least 10.
The test cannot be done, because the volunteers were not randomly sampled from a population.
The test is not appropriate, because 130 volunteers is not less than 10% of any population.
The large counts condition is not met, because 28 is less than 30.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: A random sample of 200 residents of a city is classified by age group (3 groups) and by usual transportation mode (4 modes). Which hypotheses are appropriate for a chi-square test?

choices.t: H0: In the sample, the proportion using each mode is the same in every age group. Ha: In the sample, the proportions differ.
H0: The four transportation modes are equally likely. Ha: The four transportation modes are not equally likely.
H0: Age group and transportation mode are independent in the population of residents. Ha: Age group and transportation mode are not independent.
H0: Age group and transportation mode are independent. Ha: Age group and transportation mode are positively correlated.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: A quality manager takes independent random samples of 100 items from each of three plants and classifies each item by defect type (4 types). Which hypotheses are appropriate for a chi-square test?

choices.t: H0: Defect type and plant are independent. Ha: Defect type and plant are not independent.
H0: In the samples, the distribution of defect types is the same for each plant. Ha: In the samples, the distributions differ.
H0: The mean number of defects is the same at the three plants. Ha: At least one mean is different.
H0: The distribution of defect types is the same in the populations of items from the three plants. Ha: The distribution of defect types is not the same in all three populations.

subject: AP Statistics
stem:
A chi-square test is planned for the table below, from a random sample of 70 people classified by group (rows) and response (columns).
| | Response 1 | Response 2 | Response 3 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Group 1 | 12 | 18 | 10 | 40 |
| Group 2 | 5 | 9 | 16 | 30 |
| Total | 17 | 27 | 26 | 70 |
Which statement about the expected count for Group 2, Response 1 and the condition is correct?

choices.t: The expected count is 5, and the condition is not met because that count is below 10.
The expected count is 10, so the condition is met.
The expected count is 7.29, but the condition requires all expected counts to be at least 10, so it is not met.
The expected count is 7.29, and all expected counts are at least 5, so the condition is met.

subject: AP Statistics
stem: A random sample of 90 students is classified by grade (rows: Freshman 40, Sophomore 30, Junior 20) and by whether they own a car (columns: Yes 70, No 20), with observed counts Freshman 30 and 10, Sophomore 22 and 8, Junior 18 and 2. Which statement about the expected count for Junior, No and the large counts condition is correct?

choices.t: The expected count equals the observed count of 2, which is less than 5, so the condition is not met.
The expected count is 4.44, but the condition only requires that observed counts be at least 5, so it is met.
The expected count is 4.44, which is less than 5, so the condition is not met.
The expected count is 10, so the condition is met.
